result.title: Group Relative Policy Optimisation Improves Multilingual Speech Recognition in Low-Resource Languages
result.summary: Autoregressive encoder-decoder speech recognition models trained with teacher forcing can suffer from exposure bias, limiting their ability to recover from their own prediction errors at inference time. Recent work has shown that reinforcement learning with Group Relative Policy Optimisation (GRPO) improves speech recognition in major languages with LLM-based models. We extend this line of work to smaller, non-LLM encoder-decoder ASR models, using Whisper-large-v3 as a case study across 51 African languages. The benefits of this approach are most pronounced when training data is scarce or when input audio is noisy or degraded. Our resulting model, SunflowerASR, achieves the best published macro-averaged WER on the AfriVox-v2 (0.227) and SimbaBench (0.372) benchmarks, and is publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 该文将 GRPO 强化学习后训练扩展到非 LLM 的小型 encoder-decoder 语音识别模型，以 Whisper-large-v3 在 51 种非洲语言上验证，发现低资源与噪声条件下收益最大，并发布 SunflowerASR。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属纯语音任务，但其用组内相对优势缓解 AR 解码的 exposure bias、提升模型自我纠错，可为 LVR 中 latent 轨迹的序列级贡献分配与训练监督提供核查线索。
